claims.title: How do the filtration jumps control both Frobenius matrices?
claims.hypotheses: For one integral de Rham frame of height N and a filtration-adapted invariant basis for the same local representation, all filtration degrees hⱼ lie in [−H,H]. The compatible period datum identifies the invariant subfield with the local field.
claims.statement: In the de Rham field the two evaluated Frobenius matrices have exponents N+hⱼ and N−hⱼ between inverse integral changes of basis. If H≤N both matrices are divisible by the uniformizer to power N−H in the positive de Rham ring.

claims.title: How does divisibility return to the integral coefficient ring?
claims.hypotheses: The chosen Eisenstein polynomial generates the kernel of the integral evaluation to the local ring of integers. Its image η generates the kernel of Fontaine’s map.
claims.statement: For an element of the Breuil–Kisin coefficient ring, divisibility by Eᵐ is equivalent to divisibility by ηᵐ after integral evaluation and to divisibility by the corresponding power of the de Rham uniformizer after completion.

claims.title: How does one change the height while preserving the Galois action?
claims.hypotheses: An integral de Rham frame and its adapted basis are available, with jumps bounded in absolute value by H. The period evaluation maps take the relevant factors to nonzero elements in domains.
claims.statement: There exists a frame of height H with the same Witt period matrix and the same integral Galois corrections as the initial frame. Its de Rham tests and any crystalline condition are preserved.

claims.title: How much can we divide out in two dimensions?
claims.hypotheses: In the polynomial model use diagonal exponents N+hⱼ and N−hⱼ and a triangular unimodular change of columns. The trivial representation supplies a separate period frame.
claims.statement: With N=4 and h=(−1,1), both matrices have least entry order three. Dividing each by the third power gives product t²I. A trivial Galois representation gives a genuine frame reducing to height zero.

claims.title: Why does the crystalline correction reduce to the identity?
claims.hypotheses: A crystalline period seed with trivial initial corrections supplies an integral frame and a compatible change of basis on the closed disc. The constant term of E is ℓ times a unit.
claims.statement: Every integral Galois correction of the resulting frame agrees with the identity modulo the evaluated coefficient variable.

claims.title: How do we construct a de Rham witness at a prescribed precision?
claims.hypotheses: A period seed has simultaneous logarithmic approximations for its correction κ at every order. On the coefficient disc a unit matrix changes κ to the Frobenius transform of the integral frame correction.
claims.statement: For every precision n one integral matrix β is scalar modulo E and satisfies the de Rham congruence modulo ηⁿ for every group element. Its scalar is an ℓ-power that may depend on n.

claims.title: Why can every layer use the same frame height?
claims.hypotheses: The integral local representation is continuous, its rationalization semistable, and its filtered de Rham periods are full at −H and zero at H+1 in the compatible period data.
claims.statement: Each such layer has a height-H de Rham frame which is crystalline if the rational representation is crystalline. The same filtration bound gives one height for the entire tower.
